disclosure: AI-assisted planning estimates for substantive team and operator review
case_provenance: Supplied Zertex_Case1_Technology_Product.pdf, pages 1-2, fictional Saryarqa Routes case. The main task read all three pages and visually inspected the source. Substantive team review remains pending.
assumptions_and_limitations: All costs, conversion rates, traffic, channel mix, tour margins, capacity and seasonality are unvalidated planning assumptions, not observed company results or supplier quotes.
Forecast dates are illustrative. Year 1 is January-December 2027; Year 2 is January-December 2028, the second full 12-month period from assumed kickoff.
960 paid initial-work hours are spread over approximately 12 weeks. Rates are estimated all-in cash fees, not a claim about tax treatment or local salary benchmarks.
Contingency equals 15% of initial work plus first-year running costs, excluding marketing and tour delivery. The full reserve is conservatively treated as a cash outflow in Month 3.

Gross first-year cash uses include initial work, running costs, marketing, full contingency, incremental tour delivery, payment and variable service. This is stricter than the case's development-and-launch ceiling.

Revenue and incremental delivery costs settle in the travel month. No advance-payment float, refundable customer balance, cash savings, debt, financing interest, tax benefit or legacy revenue is claimed. Tax and settlement terms need operator validation.
The funnel forecasts new completed travelers only. Existing customers moving online produce no incremental revenue in this model.

Year 2 qualified sessions increase 8.33 times from the pilot. 80% of visits are assumed earned, direct, referral or partner traffic, with no secured partnerships claimed. The remaining 20% are paid visits funded by the single marketing line.
Scale only after measured cohort conversion, delivery margin and support capacity justify it. Year 2 traffic and 90% foreign mix are ambitious hypotheses, not a forecast guarantee.

Capacity uses a planning group size of 12, four guide-days per departure including buffer, and about 25 freelancers available 12 days per month. Guide skills, language, locations, transport and dates are not verified commitments.
The 44,000 KZT case average is used for every forecast traveler. Tour-specific prototype prices are synthetic and do not feed this model.
Fractional monthly traveler counts are expected forecast values, not literal reservations. Scenario ratios are calculated before rounding.

The downside reduces incremental completed travelers by exactly 30% at the same price and mix. All project fixed costs, marketing and contingency remain unchanged. Variable costs fall with completed travelers.

Foreign share uses baseline plus incremental foreign travelers divided by all baseline plus incremental travelers for Year 2 only. The approximately 4% foreign baseline is derived from the approximate 96% domestic share.
Payback is the first monthly cumulative incremental project cash flow at or above zero within 24 months. No extrapolated date is provided when it is not reached.
